articles.title: Android 17 QPR3 Beta 1 Arrives With 20-Plus Pixel Fixes
articles.excerpt: Google's first QPR3 beta targets Pixel 6a and newer, drops the Pixel 6 and 6 Pro, and carries early code pointing to gamepad cursor control and phone-to-device unlock.
articles.image_caption: Image: @MishaalRahman via X
articles.nri_angle: The fixed eSIM self-disable bug is a genuine win for readers who toggle between a US line and a local eSIM while traveling; the beta's feature hints matter most to Pixel's enthusiast base, which includes many in the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Global Factory Output Hits Four-Year High as AI Demand Lifts Manufacturing PMIs Worldwide
articles.excerpt: September PMI data shows the broadest industrial expansion since early 2022, led by euro zone factories and Asia's chip-exporting economies.
articles.image_caption: A semiconductor fabrication plant. Global factory output hit a four-year high as AI demand lifted manufacturing
articles.nri_angle: The AI-driven factory expansion touches India's semiconductor and manufacturing ambitions as global chip and equipment demand accelerates.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infosys Extends ABN AMRO Tie-Up to Push Enterprise-Wide AI in Dutch Banking
articles.excerpt: The renewal brings Infosys Topaz's generative and agentic AI into ABN AMRO's core systems — announced a day after the stock hit a 52-week low.
articles.image_caption: The Infosys logo on a company sign. Infosys extended its strategic collaboration with ABN AMRO on September 30 to simplify the Dutch bank’s IT landscape and push enterprise-wide AI adoption.
articles.nri_angle: India's IT flagship is moving from AI pilots to enterprise-wide AI inside a major European bank even as the market punishes the stock (down 38% YTD) — a tension that defines the careers of millions of Indian tech professionals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Sends Four AI Chips Into Orbit as Project Suncatcher's First Test Takes Flight
articles.excerpt: A Planet-built prototype carrying four Trillium TPUs launched October 1 on SpaceX's Transporter-18 — the first step in Google's research into whether AI can run in space.
articles.image_caption: Google's illuminated logo. Google sent four Trillium TPUs aboard a Planet-built satellite on October 1 as the first hardware test of Project Suncatcher.
articles.nri_angle: India's own TakeMe2Space is launching an orbital computing satellite on a SpaceX rocket this year — the diaspora's space-tech ambitions are converging with Google's on the same orbital infrastructure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Will Restrict Free and AI Plus Users to Fewer Gemini Models From October 9
articles.excerpt: Free users lose Flash and Pro access; AI Plus loses Pro. But AI Pro subscribers at $19.99/month gain Deep Think reasoning — previously locked behind $99.99 Ultra plans.
articles.image_caption: Google's Mountain View headquarters. From October 9, free Gemini app users will be limited to the Flash-Lite model.
articles.nri_angle: The free-tier squeeze hits hardest for students and early-career developers — including India's large tech community — who rely on free AI tools for coding help and study.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Takes on Microsoft With ChatGPT's Own Office Suite at DevDay
articles.excerpt: At DevDay in San Francisco, OpenAI unveiled Space, Pages, and collaborative slides — workplace tools that put the ChatGPT maker in direct competition with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. The company announced Space, Pages and collaborative slides inside ChatGPT at DevDay in San Francisco.
articles.nri_angle: For the large Indian diaspora workforce in American tech, the change is practical: documents and decks where distributed teams collaborate are becoming the place where AI agents operate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wipro Merges VLSI Design Subsidiary Into IT Services Arm
articles.excerpt: Wipro has merged its US chip-design subsidiary, formerly Eximius Design, into its IT services entity effective October 1, 2026, continuing its drive to simplify the group structure. There is no cash consideration and no change in shareholding.
articles.image_caption: Wipro has merged its VLSI design subsidiary Wipro VLSI Design Services into Wipro IT Services
articles.nri_angle: Wipro is NYSE-listed and widely held by Indian-American investors, and the absorbed unit traces back to a Silicon Valley semiconductor firm founded by an Indian immigrant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft Expands Circular Centers to Give Retired Azure Servers New Life
articles.excerpt: Eight Circular Centers across three continents now securely decommission retired Azure hardware, hitting a 92% reuse and recycling rate as the AI buildout accelerates.
articles.image_caption: A data center aisle of server racks, in a Microsoft graphic about the Azure hardware lifecycle. Circular Centers process decommissioned servers and components from Microsoft's global fleet, reaching a 92% reuse and recycling rate last year.
articles.nri_angle: Indian cloud-infrastructure engineers staff much of the global Azure data-center workforce, and Indian enterprises on Azure gain verifiable hardware-reuse metrics for ESG reporting.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: At 17, Navya Tuteja Built an AI Platform to Help Neurodivergent Job Seekers
articles.excerpt: The Thomas Jefferson High School senior wrote the algorithm for Raaha herself — and did it at a school where ChatGPT and Claude are blocked on the Wi-Fi.
articles.nri_angle: Navya Tuteja, an Indian-origin teen, is already lobbying state lawmakers and the US Department of Education on AI transparency — a sign of Indian-American youth moving from tech achievement into tech policymaking.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IAF Signs Rs 135 Crore Deal With Delhi Startup for Mirage 2000 Simulators
articles.excerpt: Threye Interactive, a NewSpace Research subsidiary founded by former IAF Mirage pilot Sameer Joshi, will deliver VR-based part-task trainers for the fighter fleet after winning an iDEX challenge.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora technologists and investors, the deal shows India's iDEX pipeline producing bankable exits — a startup that began with a Mirage PC game now holds a real training contract with the IAF.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian IT Shift: Routine Jobs Face AI Pressure, Specialist Skills in Demand
articles.excerpt: Large-scale layoffs are behind Indian IT, recruiters say, but targeted exits and selective backfilling are reshaping hiring — with AI fluency now the decisive dividing line.
articles.image_caption: India's IT services industry faces pressure as AI automates routine coding jobs.
articles.nri_angle: NRI tech professionals face the same AI-driven restructuring seen in Indian IT; the premium accrues to engineers who can orchestrate AI systems rather than perform tasks within them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sarvam AI's Saaras V4 Brings Speech Recognition to All 22 Indian Languages
articles.excerpt: The Bengaluru startup's new speech-to-text model covers 22 Indian languages plus English from a single 3-billion-parameter system, and claims it beats much larger global models on Indian speech.
articles.image_caption: A branded graphic for Saaras V4, Sarvam AI's new speech-to-text model. It covers all 22 scheduled Indian languages plus global English from a single 3-billion-parameter system.
articles.nri_angle: Cheaper, India-built voice AI for the diaspora's India-facing businesses, and a home-grown benchmark for Indian engineers working on speech at US labs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TakeMe2Space to Launch India's First Orbital Computing Satellite on SpaceX Rocket
articles.excerpt: Hyderabad startup TakeMe2Space's sub-50 kg MOI-1A satellite, carrying Nvidia Orin NX edge processors, flies on SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission on October 1 with 23 customers signed.
articles.image_caption: TakeMe2Space's sub-50 kg MOI-1A satellite carries Nvidia Orin NX edge-computing processors and a 9-band multispectral imager. It is scheduled to launch on SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission on October 1.
articles.nri_angle: With US firms already signed as customers and Indian-origin engineers prominent in global space-tech, TakeMe2Space's orbital-compute bet gives diaspora professionals a new India-built capability to watch.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Unveils Gemini 4 Argon, Its Most Powerful AI Model Yet
articles.excerpt: The first Gemini 4 model targets long, multi-step engineering and cybersecurity work, leads on 13 of 18 benchmarks by Google's count, and rolls out first to trusted cyber defenders — with broader access to follow.
articles.image_caption: The Googleplex, Google's headquarters in Mountain View, California
articles.nri_angle: Google CEO Sundar Pichai's Gemini 4 Argon launch is a defining test for the Tamil Nadu-born chief executive — and for the vast Indian engineering workforce that powers Google's AI ambitions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Pricing Pressure and Cautious Clients Cloud Indian IT's September Quarter Earnings
articles.excerpt: Five brokerages tell Reuters that India's top IT firms face their weakest sequential quarter in three years as AI-driven price deflation eats into the billable-hours model; guidance cuts loom when TCS reports October 8.
articles.image_caption: A data card from analyst Aravind Raghunathan shows the Jefferies forecast of 0.7% to 3.5% quarter-on-quarter revenue growth for India's top six IT firms. The figure would mark the sector's weakest sequential performance in three years as AI-driven pricing pressure and cautious client spending weigh on September-quarter earnings.
articles.nri_angle: India's IT sector anchors diaspora jobs, visa-linked postings, and NRI investment; its forced pivot from billable hours to AI-driven outcomes reshapes prospects for Indian tech professionals at home and abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IT Fresher Hiring Rebounds After Five-Year Slide as Agrani Lines Up Rs 800 Crore Raise
articles.excerpt: TCS, Infosys and HCLTech hired about 19,000 entry-level staff in the June quarter as annual intake climbs back from its FY26 low — while semiconductor startup Agrani Labs negotiates a Rs 800-850 crore round led by Peak XV, Samsung and 360 One.
articles.image_caption: An illustration showing job candidates beneath a HIRING sign. Entry-level hiring by India's top IT firms is rebounding after annual fresher intake fell from 380,000 in FY22 to about 110,000 in FY26.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian tech diaspora, the hiring rebound signals a healthier talent pipeline feeding global delivery centres — and the Agrani raise shows Bengaluru semiconductor bets drawing Korean and global capital, not just domestic funds.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After the Clarity Act Stalled, US Regulators Are Writing Crypto Rules Themselves
articles.excerpt: Days after the Senate's 49-50 vote, the SEC opened a path for tokenized stocks and the CFTC sent a crypto rule to the White House.
articles.image_caption: Digital currency imagery used in coverage of US crypto policy. The Senate blocked the Clarity Act on September 15, pushing the SEC and CFTC to advance crypto rules on their own.
articles.nri_angle: The US crypto rulebook shapes where diaspora founders build; India's own holding-pattern policy is calibrated partly against Washington's moves.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 23-Year-Old Dropout's AI Assistant Is Taking On Zuckerberg's Meta
articles.excerpt: Instinct, built by Noah Shinn, is reportedly raising $1 billion at a $10 billion valuation — weeks after Meta launched its rival, Muse.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin researchers and investors sit on both sides of the AI-assistant race, from model labs to the Sequoia and Benchmark partnerships.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Agents Breached Retailers for $25 Apiece and Stole 600,000 Credit Cards
articles.excerpt: Gambit Security's reconstruction of a months-long campaign shows autonomous hacking tools collapsing the cost of cybercrime.
articles.image_caption: Hackers work at a bank of monitors in a dark operations room. Attackers used AI agents to breach retailers for as little as $25 apiece, stealing 600,000 credit card numbers in days.
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT firms defend global retail clients facing the same skimmer threat; India's e-commerce and semiconductor push raise the domestic stakes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google's $899 Googlebooks Bet on Android Loyalty Faces the Real Test
articles.excerpt: Google's Android-based Googlebooks start at $899 in October with Gemini AI baked in — but the real question is whether a billion Android users will trust Google with their laptop.
articles.image_caption: A Googlebook laptop. Google’s new Android-based laptops start at $899 and launch in October, with Gemini AI built into the operating system.
articles.nri_angle: India, overwhelmingly an Android market, is where the loyalty Googlebooks needs lives — whether students, developers and professionals there buy into a Google-centric laptop will decide the product's fate as much as US reception.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infosys Cleared in AI Worker's 'Sham' Contract Case in Australia
articles.excerpt: Australia's Fair Work Commission ruled the AI expert's engagement was a standard three-way labour-hire arrangement, rejecting her claim that Infosys was her true employer.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling carries weight for Indian tech professionals in Australia, many of whom work through labour-hire chains on sponsored visas — and now know host companies carry legal distance in dismissal claims.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's 'AI 100' Names 100 Agency Leaders Reshaping Brands With AI
articles.excerpt: Indian Startup Times has published "The AI 100: Agency Leaders Redefining Brands with AI," an editorial list recognizing 100 agency and marketing leaders across India who are bringing artificial intelligence into brand building — from creative technologists and prompt-engineering-certified tech leads to veteran media planners.
articles.image_caption: A photo collage of headshots of Indian advertising and marketing leaders, arranged around the Indian Startup Times logo. Indian Startup Times uses the collage for its editorial list features recognizing leaders across India's agency and marketing ecosystem.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora in marketing and advertising abroad, the AI 100 maps India-based counterparts operating at the same scale — including Publicis Global Delivery leaders running global media operations from India — and sits alongside TIME100 AI 2026's ten Indian-origin honorees as a marker of Indian AI talent's global footprint.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Soul-Sucking' AI Coding Post Goes Viral as Elon Musk, Top Tech Leaders Weigh In
articles.excerpt: An anonymous engineer's X post describing his Claude Code-driven job as 'soul-sucking' — 'Nobody knows anything here,' he wrote — drew millions of views and responses from Elon Musk, Chamath Palihapitiya, and GitLab's CEO, reopening the debate over what AI is doing to software work.
articles.image_caption: A visitor walks past a large illuminated AI sign at a technology exhibition. The viral post argued that AI coding tools have reduced engineers to button-pushers, drawing responses from Elon Musk and other tech leaders.
articles.nri_angle: India's vast software workforce — including thousands of diaspora engineers at US tech companies — faces the same AI-driven productivity pressure the viral post describes, making the debate over developer agency and deskilling deeply personal for the community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The IIT Delhi Engineer Behind Apple's Foldable iPhone Duo
articles.excerpt: Piyush Pratik, an IIT Delhi graduate turned Apple product manager, holds a leadership role on the iPhone Duo — Apple's first foldable iPhone and its most expensive model ever.
articles.image_caption: Piyush Pratik, an Apple product manager for iPhone. His LinkedIn profile lists him as Product Manager, iPhone Duo, placing him in the leadership team for Apple's first foldable iPhone, unveiled on September 9, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: An IIT Delhi alumnus now holds a leadership role on Apple's most ambitious iPhone in years — a visible marker of how central Indian-origin engineers have become to flagship Silicon Valley hardware.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian American Founders Raise $24 Million to Build AI Workforce for Lenders
articles.excerpt: Kastle's Series A round, led by Insight Partners, will fund AI agents that work across banks' existing systems. Co-founders Rishi Choudhary and Nitish Poddar say the agents have already processed $1.8 billion in transactions.
articles.image_caption: The San Francisco financial district. Kastle, a San Francisco startup founded by Rishi Choudhary and Nitish Poddar, raised $24 million in Series A funding led by Insight Partners to build AI agents for consumer lenders.
articles.nri_angle: Kastle was founded by Indian American entrepreneurs Rishi Choudhary and Nitish Poddar, continuing the diaspora's strong presence in enterprise AI and fintech leadership.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Swiss Physicists Fire 'Atomic Cannon' to Test Einstein's Gravity Rule
articles.excerpt: Researchers at ETH Zurich and the Paul Scherrer Institute have produced an intense, precisely controlled beam of muonium atoms — opening the first path to measuring gravity's pull on second-generation matter.
articles.image_caption: Two researchers align the cryogenic apparatus used to produce the muonium beam at the Paul Scherrer Institute. The beam could allow the first measurement of how gravity acts on matter dominated by a second-generation particle.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AMD Crosses $1 Trillion as Meta's Muse AI Agent Ignites Chip Rally
articles.excerpt: Intel jumped 12% and Arm surged 17% on Monday as the runaway success of Meta's Muse assistant convinced investors that AI agents will drive a surge in demand for central processing units.
articles.image_caption: AMD's headquarters in Santa Clara, California. The chipmaker's market capitalization crossed $1 trillion on Monday as a broad semiconductor rally, set off by Meta's runaway Muse AI agent, pushed Intel and Arm to double-digit gains.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers make up a large share of the semiconductor workforce at AMD, Intel and Arm in Silicon Valley and India's chip-design hubs, and U.S.-listed equities have become a growing allocation for Indian retail investors through cross-border investing apps — so the CPU rally lands close to home for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oracle Layoffs Hit Abilene, the 'Flagship' Site of Its OpenAI Stargate Deal
articles.excerpt: The Times of India reports the layoffs have reached the flagship Stargate data center in Abilene, Texas — the site Oracle keeps citing as proof its OpenAI deal is on track — as the company cuts up to 30,000 jobs to fund a $50 billion AI buildout.
articles.image_caption: Oracle's headquarters. Layoffs hit the company's Abilene, Texas site, the flagship of its OpenAI Stargate deal.
articles.nri_angle: Oracle employs thousands of Indian engineers in the US and India, and reported India cuts of ~3,000 jobs make this layoff wave a direct bread-and-butter concern for the diaspora tech workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Stellantis Takes Full Control of Thiruvallur Plant, Targets 160% Output Jump
articles.excerpt: The automaker bought out CK Birla Group's stake in its 2017 joint venture and will more than double the Tamil Nadu plant's workforce as it ramps output toward 50,000 units, with exports taking the lead.
articles.image_caption: A Stellantis plant. The automaker has taken full control of its Thiruvallur facility and targets a 160% output jump.
articles.nri_angle: Stellantis's export-led expansion widens opportunities for Indian-origin auto engineers and underscores India's manufacturing story for diaspora investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Cuts Fitness+ Audio Jobs in Second Layoff Round in Two Months
articles.excerpt: The cuts hit the audio team behind Time to Walk and Time to Run and come amid reports the workout service may eventually fold into a redesigned Health app.
articles.image_caption: An Apple marketing image shows Fitness+ workout sessions playing across an iPad, iPhone, and Apple Watch, with on-screen workout metrics. Apple cut a “handful” of Fitness+ roles this past week, its second round of layoffs in less than two months, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals are heavily represented across Apple's software and health teams, so restructuring inside Cupertino lands close to home — while the Apple Watch health ecosystem remains a staple of health-conscious Indian-American families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Musk Pitches 200-Mph Hyperloop Tunnel Between Austin and San Antonio
articles.excerpt: The Boring Company founder says the 80-mile Texas tunnel would cut a drive that can take 2.5 hours to under 30 minutes — but revealed no route, cost, or timeline.
articles.image_caption: Elon Musk, in a dark suit and tie, steps out of an elevator. Musk said on Sunday that The Boring Company is working on a 200-mph “precursor Hyperloop” tunnel between Austin and San Antonio.
articles.image_credit: Benjamin Fanjoy / Getty Images via TechCrunch
articles.nri_angle: Austin's booming Indian tech community — thousands of Indian engineers across Tesla, SpaceX, Boring, and X in nearby Bastrop — sits directly on the corridor Musk wants to tunnel under, making this Texas infrastructure bet a local story for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vaishnaw warns chip industry to brace for cyberattacks as India's semiconductor push accelerates
articles.excerpt: The Electronics and IT minister says India's new chip-making capability will be seen as a threat by established players, even as five units reach commercial production and global CEOs finalise India investments.
articles.image_caption: Ashwini Vaishnaw. The Union minister warned the chip industry to brace for cyberattacks as India's semiconductor push accelerates.
articles.nri_angle: India's chip push is drawing investment and talent globally, and a secure, credible semiconductor ecosystem gives diaspora engineers and startup founders a serious reason to build with India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
